title: Copenhagen at Chichester - review
transcript: Copenhagen by Michael Frayn at Chichester Festival Theatre Minerva theatre so what is Copenhagen about it's about a mysterious meeting that took place in the Danish capital during World War two between two of the great quantum theorists Heisenberg II of the uncertainty principle and Bohr who United the two main theories of quantum mechanics yes but what's it really about it plays about three dead people Heisenberg Bohr and for his wife trying to work out between them what happened back in 1942 they keep going over the same ground but with different results and along the way reveal all sorts of interesting things well the play is about quantum theory in the place structure it's dialogue and Michael Blake more stark production contribute to our understanding of that the play is about history and science and how the to interlink quantum theory led to nuclear fission which led to the atomic bomb and a race between Germany and the Allies to create the atomic bomb the play is about the moral dilemma felt by a theoretical scientist wanted to help win a war but working on a weapon of mass destruction to achieve that victory the plays about the impossibilities of seeing yourself objectively and how what happened is always gone and replaced by an unreliable memory influenced by subsequent events the plays about how people and relationships affect history and science how jealousy rivalry fear ambition personal tragedy play their part Charles Edward says Heisenberg gives a movie account of life under the Nazis but Patricia Hodge important are his equal in acting power the play is about how an intelligent well-written drama can explain all this using exhilarating witty dialogue and to go back to quantum theory the play is about how the acts of observation changes what's being observed now it might have been different on a different night but when I observed it I thought Copenhagen at the Minerva deserved five stars you
